encounters.cc: Persistent fatigue, excessive thirst, frequent urination, and unintentional weight loss of 6 kg over the past month.

lines: Persistent fatigue, excessive thirst, frequent urination, and unintentional weight loss of 6 kg over the past month.
Over the past month, he has been waking up multiple times during the night to urinate and has begun carrying a water bottle with him everywhere.
He reports drinking nearly 5 liters of water daily.
Despite a markedly increased appetite, he has lost 6 kg (13 lb) unintentionally over the same period.
He also reports intermittent blurry vision over the past week, especially when reading or using his laptop.
He denies any dysuria, urgency, or abdominal pain.
- Recurrent herpes simplex virus type 1 infection
- Insulin glargine 16 units subcutaneous at bedtime
- Insulin lispro Sliding scale with meals
- Valacyclovir 500 mg orally twice daily as needed for oral lesions
He does not use drugs, alcohol, or tobacco.
There is no fever, rash, or joint pain.
Blood pressure is 106/64 mm Hg, pulse is 92/min, and temperature is normal.
On physical exam, he is thin and appears slightly dehydrated.
Visual acuity is mildly reduced but improves temporarily with blinking.
Genitourinary and neurologic exams are unremarkable.
The clinician suspects a metabolic condition

encounters.cc: Mild jaundice with yellowing of skin and eyes for 2 days; reports similar episodes during illness or stress over the past year.

lines: Mild jaundice with yellowing of skin and eyes for 2 days; reports similar episodes during illness or stress over the past year.
The patient returns for Gastroenterology follow-up with known Dubin-Johnson syndrome and Gilbert syndrome, presenting with recurrent jaundice six months after diabetes diagnosis.
He reports that the yellowing of his skin and eyes seems to come and go, and he has noticed similar episodes a few times over the past year, usually during times of illness or stress.
He denies pruritus, abdominal pain, dark urine, or pale stools.
- Recurrent herpes simplex virus type 1 infection
- Insulin glargine 16 units subcutaneous at bedtime
- Insulin lispro Sliding scale with meals
- Valacyclovir 500 mg orally twice daily as needed for oral lesions
His mother has a history of similar symptoms but has never been formally diagnosed with a liver disorder.
He does not smoke, drink alcohol, or use illicit drugs.
Physical examination reveals scleral icterus and a slightly tender liver edge, but no other abnormalities.

lines: Yellowing of skin and eyes for 2 days during final examination period with poor sleep and irregular eating.

He reports no pain, pruritus, or changes in stool or urine color.

- Recurrent herpes simplex virus type 1 infection

His abdomen is soft, non-tender, and without hepatosplenomegaly.

encounters.cc: Yellowing of eyes noticed over past two days, one week after undergoing laparoscopic appendectomy.

lines: Yellowing of eyes noticed over past two days, one week after undergoing laparoscopic appendectomy.

The patient returns for postoperative follow-up with known Gilbert syndrome and Dubin-Johnson syndrome, having presented previously in 2021 with similar episodes of scleral icterus during examination periods.
He presents to clinic one week after undergoing a laparoscopic appendectomy for uncomplicated acute appendicitis.
He reports that he has been recovering well overall but noticed that the whites of his eyes appeared yellow over the past two days.
He has no abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, or changes in bowel movements.
His appetite has improved since surgery, and he is passing gas and tolerating oral intake.
He denies fever, chills, dark urine, or pale stools.
- Recurrent herpes simplex virus type 1 infection
Taking only acetaminophen for occasional discomfort.
- Insulin glargine 16 units subcutaneous at bedtime
- Insulin lispro Sliding scale with meals
- Valacyclovir 500 mg orally twice daily as needed for oral lesions
His family history is notable for his father having “some liver enzyme issue” that was never treated.
Smoking: Never smoker. Alcohol: None. Occupation: Undergraduate student.
On review of systems, he reports feeling a little fatigued but otherwise well.
Scleral icterus is present, but his skin is not jaundiced.
His abdomen is soft and non-tender with healed incisions and no signs of fluid collection.
Total bilirubin of 3.1 mg/dL with indirect bilirubin of 2.8 mg/dL, direct bilirubin of 0.3 mg/dL, normal AST, ALT, and alkaline phosphatase, and normal hemoglobin and hematocrit.

encounters.cc: Painful sores on lips and inside mouth for 3 days with mild fever, preceded by tingling sensation.

lines: Painful sores on lips and inside mouth for 3 days with mild fever, preceded by tingling sensation.
The patient, a 25-year-old male with recurrent HSV-1 infection and Gilbert syndrome with stress-induced flares, presents with perioral lesions.
He reports feeling a tingling sensation in the area before the blisters appeared.
This has happened several times in the past, usually during periods of stress or lack of sleep.
The lesions are limited to the perioral region and are associated with mild fever.
- Recurrent herpes simplex virus type 1 infection
- Insulin glargine 16 units subcutaneous at bedtime
- Insulin lispro Sliding scale with meals
- Valacyclovir 500 mg orally twice daily as needed for oral lesions
Smoking: Never smoker. Alcohol: None. Occupation: Undergraduate student.

encounters.cc: Yellowing of eyes noticed by roommate this morning after returning from a five-day camping trip with irregular meals.

lines: Yellowing of eyes noticed by roommate this morning after returning from a five-day camping trip with irregular meals.

The patient is a 26-year-old male with Gilbert syndrome and Dubin-Johnson syndrome who returns with recurrent jaundice, having experienced similar episodes during examination periods in 2021 and following appendectomy in 2022.
He denies any abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, fatigue, weight loss, pruritus, or dark urine.
He reports that he just returned from a five-day camping trip during which he had irregular meals and ate very little due to limited access to food.
He notes feeling mildly tired since getting back but attributes this to dehydration and lack of sleep.
He denies recent infections, alcohol use, drug use, or any new medications or supplements.
He recalls having a similar episode of yellowing in college after pulling several all-nighters for exams and skipping meals for a couple of days.
At that time, he felt well otherwise and the yellowing resolved on its own without intervention.
- Recurrent herpes simplex virus type 1 infection
He does not take any regular medications.
- Insulin glargine 16 units subcutaneous at bedtime
- Insulin lispro Sliding scale with meals
- Valacyclovir 500 mg orally twice daily as needed for oral lesions
Family history is notable for his younger brother experiencing similar episodes.
There is no history of liver disease, gallstones, or autoimmune conditions in the family.
Smoking: Never smoker. Alcohol: None. Occupation: Undergraduate student.
Vitals are within normal limits, BMI is 22
On physical exam, the patient appears well and is in no acute distress.
Scleral icterus is present but there is no jaundice of the skin.
There is no hepatomegaly or splenomegaly on abdominal palpation, and the liver span is normal to percussion.
There are no spider angiomas, palmar erythema, ascites, or other stigmata of chronic liver disease.
Neurologic and cardiopulmonary exams are unremarkable.

encounters.cc: Lightheadedness, dizziness, and nausea for the past hour after participating in a soccer tournament during hot summer weather.

lines: Lightheadedness, dizziness, and nausea for the past hour after participating in a soccer tournament during hot summer weather.
The patient has Type 1 diabetes mellitus, Gilbert syndrome, and Dubin-Johnson syndrome, with recurrent jaundice episodes most recently in January 2024.
He presents to the emergency department in July after participating in a soccer tournament.
He reports that he has been playing soccer for the past three hours in the hot sun without any breaks.
He has been drinking water throughout the day but has not eaten much.
- Recurrent herpes simplex virus type 1 infection
- Insulin glargine 16 units subcutaneous at bedtime
- Insulin lispro Sliding scale with meals
- Valacyclovir 500 mg orally twice daily as needed for oral lesions
Smoking: Never smoker. Alcohol: None. Occupation: Undergraduate student.

His vital signs are as follows: temperature 39.5 C (103.1 F), heart rate 110 beats per minute, blood pressure 100/60 mmHg, respiratory rate 22 breaths per minute, and oxygen saturation 98% on room air.
On examination, his skin is cool and moist, and he appears fatigued but is oriented to time, place, and person.
